title: Build a DataFrame
summary: A DataFrame is a table with labelled columns and rows. Each list supplied here becomes one column.
introduction: A DataFrame is a table with labelled columns and rows. Each list supplied here becomes one column. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A DataFrame is a table with labelled columns and rows. Each list supplied here becomes one column.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Examples need Python and pandas in a separate environment. The people and scores are fictional. Do not use real learner records for practice.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Pandas. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

print(df.shape)
blocks.title: Build a DataFrame

blocks.text: The output is (3, 3). There are three rows and three columns: name, score and team.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add a fourth fictional learner to every column list.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: All column lists must have compatible lengths when building this table.
For more detail later, use this [Pandas further reading](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/getting_started/intro_tutorials/).
